question: Dysentery is defined as any diarrhoea with more than five episodes per day, regardless of whether blood or mucus is present in the stool.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. Dysentery is diarrhoea accompanied by blood and mucus in the stool with tenesmus — indicating mucosal invasion. Stool frequency alone (≥3/day) defines diarrhoea, not dysentery.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — dysentery is NOT defined by stool frequency. It specifically requires the presence of blood and mucus in the stool, typically with tenesmus, indicating mucosal invasion and inflammation. Frequency alone (≥3 loose stools/day) defines diarrhoea.
